Patricia Hearst (born 1954) is the granddaughter of American publishing magnate William Randolph Hearst. In 1974, while she was a 19-year-old student living in Berkeley, California, Hearst was abducted by a left-wing terrorist group known as the Symbionese Liberation Army. After being isolated, raped and threatened with death, she became supportive of their cause, making propaganda announcements for them and taking part in illegal activities.

Those activities included this robbery of the Hibernia Bank in San Francisco. Hearst carried an M-1 carbine rifle and announced herself under her pseudonym of Tania. Two men who entered the bank while the robbery was occurring were shot and wounded. She was later involved in another bank robbery, a shoot-out, car jackings, kidnappings and the attempted murder of two policemen with bombs.

After her arrest in September of 1975, 19 months after her abduction, she was put on trial for this robbery only. Her lawyer, F. Lee Bailey asserted a defense of coercion or duress affecting intent at the time of the offense— similar to a brainwashing-type excuse. At the time of her arrest, Patty Hearst weighed only 87 pounds and was described as "a low-IQ, low-affect zombie" and there were some clear signs of trauma and several DSM-5 classifications: her IQ was measured at 112 from 130 previously, she had been locked in a closet for extended periods of time and reportedly raped and threatened with death, there were huge gaps in her memory regarding her pre-Tania life, she was smoking heavily and had nightmares.

In March of 1976 Hearst was convicted of bank robbery and using a firearm in a felony. She was given a sentence of 7 years. President Carter commuted her sentence to the 22 months served eight months before she would have had a parole hearing. President Reagan reportedly gave serious consideration to pardoning Hearst. She recovered full rights when President Clinton granted her a pardon on January 20, 2001, his last day in office.
